text: Odds API keys: closed. The PropLine investigation (full write-up: research/propline_vs_vigilant_2026-10-16.md). Short answer: Vigilant did not miss real +EV; PropLine's +EV props are not +EV. What I measured: (1) on the 427 lines of PropLine's list that Vigilant also priced, the Novig price is the same (0.05 pts apart on props) but the FAIR differs by 8 points on props: that is Vigilant's prop haircut (-7 pts on an Over, -3 on an Under, built from your own bet history). (2) I then tested the claim directly on PropLine's resolved archive (MLB+NHL, 25,909 props, Novig's closing price vs Pinnacle's devigged close, real results): Overs that look +2% to +12% vs Pinnacle LOST 9-14% (6,400 bets; they win 3-5 points less than Pinnacle's fair). So following PropLine's prop-Over list would lose money; Vigilant refusing them is correct. Unders are roughly fair (the +EV Under sample is too small to call). (3) Game lines: Novig's price had moved 0.6-3 points since PropLine's read (its Novig read is minutes old), so PropLine's +1..3% was gone at the live price. (4) The 84 it could not match: lone-Kalshi longshots (+3000 goals, first goal) and far-away NCAAF alt lines. Fix shipped in code: the PropLine +EV screen now shows the edge AFTER Vigilant's prop cut and ranks/filters on it, with a line saying what PropLine claimed. Next: I'm building the PropLine grading, hit-rate and line-movement features (TCL56d).
